literaryAssessment.charactersAndActions: Named characters act through recruitment, danger, rescue, bargaining, loss and return. The failed burglary, Beorn introductions, wet barrel ride and home auction carry real comic or atmospheric texture. No modern competence/leadership exercises survive.
literaryAssessment.relationships: Bilbo’s initial doubt and Gandalf’s advocacy, Thorin’s jewel attachment and Bilbo’s return despite warning are retained. Reconciliation is attributed to Thorin rather than converted into the digest writer’s lesson. The chronology finding damages that last relationship beat; optional T02 describes further thinness without inventing a confrontation.
literaryAssessment.uncertaintyAndReflection: The tentative settled-at-home opening is preserved. Final Gandalf reflection remains attributed and does not import Foster’s providential theology as settled fact. The unsupported collective ignorance in l-arkenstone needs narrowing.
literaryAssessment.battlePerspective: Before the knockout, battle action follows the checked chapter-17 outline; after it, the account is explicitly reported to Bilbo, not invented eyewitness narration. HOB-SR-002 corrects its placement.
literaryAssessment.ruEnParity: All 35 pairs read substantively. No different ending or whole alternate plot found. Specific asymmetries: e-gollum assigns the proposal to Gollum in RU versus mutual agreement in EN; l-arkenstone RU adds why to the shared unverified ignorance. Both are covered by required findings.
literaryAssessment.sufficiency: The professional guides plus the actually read primary opening can support a concise modern arc. The identified clause-level evidence gaps and flow/spoiler defects prevent PASS on this candidate; absence of a full EPUB is not itself the rejection.

routes.assessment: An intelligible opening journey and honest stop at Smaug, except for the dangling troll setup.
Adds real scenes, escapes and entrapment, but discloses the decisive weak-spot mechanism and has a riddle-scene rewind.
Connected full arc with source-precision and battle-account-order corrections required.

ru.text: Впереди обнаруживаются три тролля, возле которых маленькому взломщику предстоит впервые показать, на что он способен.
На пути к горам компания добирается до Ривенделла.

en.text: Ahead are three trolls, near whom the little burglar will have his first opportunity to demonstrate his abilities.
On the way to the mountains, the company reaches Rivendell.

findings.defect: Essential sets up the imminent troll encounter, then skips both its event and its outcome. A reader follows a promised test straight into Rivendell without learning what happened. This is an internal dangling beat, not the deliberate final stop at Smaug.

smallestFaithfulCorrection.ru: Добавить к переходу в Ривенделл короткое сообщение, что из тролльего плена компанию выручил Гэндальф. Подробный голосовой трюк может остаться в Core.
smallestFaithfulCorrection.en: Add a short bridge into Rivendell stating that Gandalf rescued the company from the trolls. The detailed voice trick can stay in Core.

findings.acceptance: Read Essential continuously in both languages: the trolls must either have a brief supported outcome or cease to be a dangling setup. Keep the unresolved final dragon encounter.

ru.text: О победе ему рассказывают после пробуждения: орлы очистили склоны от гоблинов; Беорн вынес раненого Торина и убил Болга, предводителя врагов.
Теперь его ведут к Торину — тот ещё жив, но ранен смертельно.

en.text: He learns of the victory after waking: the Eagles cleared the slopes of goblins; Beorn carried out the wounded Thorin and killed Bolg, the enemy leader.
Now he is taken to Thorin, who is still alive but mortally wounded.

findings.defect: The detailed retrospective battle account is placed before Bilbo is brought to the dying Thorin. The checked guide places the deathbed encounter before the retrospective account. The current explicit Now/Теперь makes this a changed sequence, rather than neutral compression. Bilbo is correctly described as unconscious for the ending; the problem is when he hears its details.

smallestFaithfulCorrection.ru: Оставить в n-unconscious пробуждение и путь к раненому Торину; перенести сообщение об орлах, Беорне и Болге после последнего разговора, например в начало o-settlement. Не превращать его в увиденную Бильбо сцену.
smallestFaithfulCorrection.en: Keep waking and the approach to Thorin in n-unconscious. Move the reported Eagles/Beorn/Bolg account after the last conversation, for example to the opening of o-settlement. Keep it explicitly second-hand.

findings.acceptance: The continuous Deep route must preserve deathbed encounter before detailed retrospective battle explanation; no invented eyewitness battle narration.

ru.text: В разговоре Бильбо замечает незащищённое место на груди Смауга. С этим открытием он возвращается к гномам.

en.text: During their conversation Bilbo notices an unprotected patch on Smaug’s breast. He brings that discovery back to the dwarves.

findings.defect: k-bare-patch is level 2. Its title and body expose the decisive mechanism later used to kill Smaug. Outcomes themselves are correctly level 3, but the explicit review brief also reserves decisive mechanisms for warned Deep. Core consent is not Deep consent.

smallestFaithfulCorrection.ru: Сохранить для Core возвращение в туннель и ловушку, но дать нейтральный заголовок; открытие уязвимости перенести в Deep перед его использованием. Альтернатива — перенести весь экран в level 3. Затем заново вывести точные counts.
smallestFaithfulCorrection.en: Keep the retreat and entrapment in Core under a neutral title, and disclose the vulnerability in Deep before it is used. Alternatively move the whole screen to level 3. Recompute the exact nested counts.

evidence.location: Current user review brief: decisive mechanisms/ending restricted to warnedDeep; current canonical screen k-bare-patch.level = 2; collector HTML visibleScreens()/contentsHtml()

findings.acceptance: No title or body in Essential/Core reveals the decisive weak-spot mechanism. Verify Deep consent, shallow contents, Continue and Sources after the correction.

ru.text: Гэндальф подмешивает в их перебранку голоса, затягивая спор.
Последним вопросом становится случайное размышление Бильбо о собственном кармане.
Он перепрыгивает через него и спасается от гоблинов, охраняющих ворота.

en.text: Gandalf adds deceptive voices to the argument and keeps it going.
They agree to a riddle contest
The last question comes from Bilbo wondering aloud about his own pocket.
He jumps over him and escapes past the goblins guarding the gate.

evidenceMap.text: Commentary's pocket-question reference and leap/mercy discussion supply these retained event links.

findings.defect: The cited Foster HTML has no pocket-question account (its pocket reference is the ring being put away), and its metaphorical leap discussion does not describe the physical jump. It also omits the voice-throwing mechanism. The acquisition map therefore overstates what that particular source establishes. Independently checked Caroline Batten/Oxford narrative-summary pages 1–2 do support the voice trick, pocket question and physical leap; they are secondary scholarship, not Tolkien prose. Neither the supplied Foster passage nor the checked Oxford summary explicitly establishes the accidental wondering-aloud formulation or who proposes the game. RU alone assigns the proposal to Gollum.

smallestFaithfulCorrection.ru: Сохранить подтверждённые трюк, вопрос и прыжок, но честно добавить Batten/Oxford в evidence map, sources.md и экранные source IDs. Не приписывать эти детали Фостеру или Толкину как прочитанному первичному тексту. Для текущей доказательной базы убрать «случайное размышление» и нейтрально передать вопрос о содержимом кармана; RU предложение состязания передать как взаимную договорённость, как в EN, либо найти прямое подтверждение.
smallestFaithfulCorrection.en: Retain the corroborated voice trick, pocket question and leap, but add Batten/Oxford to the evidence map, source ledger and screen source IDs. Do not attribute them to the read Foster text or call the guide Tolkien’s primary prose. With the current evidence, state the pocket question neutrally without inventing its spontaneous origin; align RU with the EN mutual agreement unless the proposer is directly checked.

ru.text: Смауг отвечает подозрениями о гномах и обещанной награде.

en.text: Smaug responds with suspicions about the dwarves and their promised reward.

findings.defect: Foster chapter 12 supports a perilous conversation, indirect self-names and a general dragon tendency to sow distrust. It does not give this specific subject of Smaug’s speech about the dwarves’ promised reward. The checked Oxford summary does not supply it either. This is a narrow unsupported attribution of speech content, not a demonstrated claim that the event never occurs in the novel.

smallestFaithfulCorrection.ru: До проверки прямого соответствующего фрагмента убрать это предложение. Опасный разговор и непрямые имена Бильбо можно сохранить: они подтверждены.
smallestFaithfulCorrection.en: Omit this sentence until the relevant direct passage is checked. Retain the dangerous conversation and Bilbo’s indirect names, which are established.

evidence.location: Chapter 12, Summary and Discussion and Essay Topics (dragon characteristics; indirect names)
Narrative Summary, printed p. 2, Smaug paragraph
evidence.role: secondary summary; does not establish the reward exchange

findings.acceptance: No exact speech topic is attributed to Smaug solely from a critic’s general characterization. A precise lawful primary passage can close this clause-level gap.

ru.text: дракон исчез, но никто ещё не знает, куда и зачем он полетел.

en.text: The dragon has vanished, and they do not yet know where he has gone.
Smaug flies to take revenge on Lake-town.

findings.defect: The evidence supports Bilbo’s continuing alarm about Smaug, not the universal assertion about what nobody knows. RU additionally asserts ignorance of his reason, absent from EN. The next screen introduces revenge on Lake-town without explaining why the dragon targets that town. This manufactures uncertainty in one place while dropping the source-backed cause in the next.

smallestFaithfulCorrection.ru: В l-arkenstone оставить тревогу Бильбо: Смауг по-прежнему опасен. Убрать всеобщее «никто не знает». В Deep перед нападением коротко указать, что Смауг заподозрил помощь Озёрного города гномам; это прямо поддерживает проверенная сводка Oxford. Отразить новый источник в карте.
smallestFaithfulCorrection.en: In l-arkenstone retain Bilbo’s alarm that Smaug remains dangerous, and omit the unverified collective ignorance. Before the Deep attack, briefly state that Smaug suspected Lake-town had helped the company, as the checked Oxford summary establishes. Update the source map.

evidence.location: Chapter 13, Summary (Bilbo’s warning); Chapter 14, Summary (attack target)
Narrative Summary, printed p. 2, Smaug/Lake-town paragraph
evidence.role: secondary guide; explicit suspicion of Lake-town’s assistance

findings.acceptance: RU/EN state the same supported uncertainty. The town’s targeting has a brief established cause; no new dialogue, detailed motives or modern lesson.

optionalTaste.observation: In Core/Deep the story reaches the invisible following at the end of e-gollum, then rewinds to the last riddle and repeats invisibility/following in e-pocket. A short explicit retrospective transition, or moving the pocket question into the first screen and using the second for the merciful escape, would improve forward movement. Oxford p. 2 supports pity; it can be restored as Bilbo’s feeling rather than an external moral lesson.

evidence.location: Narrative Summary, printed p. 2, Gollum paragraph

optionalTaste.observation: The recruitment and later threatened rupture are economical but thin. The morning-discovery setup goes directly to a bargain, so the final reconciliation carries less emotional weight than it could. Any enrichment should come from checked passages; do not invent Thorin’s words, an expulsion scene or Bilbo’s motives merely to add drama. This is separate from the definite chronology finding.
